subject: Determine whether public YouTube channels and external profiles attributed to Kamilah/Camila/Camilla Stevenson can be safely treated as one creator before video inventory.

notes: YouTube search result exposes the channel name, handle and general investing description.
Direct channel/About page retrieval was disabled in this run; no first-party external links, legal name, contact email or ownership proof was captured.
Third-party analytics page identifies a different channel ID from UCXm6KAr1WHF6UN7g5b2W7wg.
A second third-party evaluator reports a different subscriber/video count for this channel; metrics are stale/inconsistent and not identity evidence.
Third-party mirror shows a finance-coach bio and Chicago location.
No first-party link from this profile to either YouTube channel was captured.
A secondary article attributes a public post to this handle.
No first-party cross-link to the YouTube channel was captured.

findings.claim: At least two distinct YouTube channel IDs are indexed under the Kamilah Stevenson name/branding.
Third-party channel metrics conflict materially: one result reports 137K, another 143K/1.2K videos, and a third 103K/633 videos.
Third-party transcript summaries attribute videos to Kamilah Stevenson while the speaker introduces herself as 'Camila Stevenson'.
No first-party website, verified social account, business registration, or creator-controlled cross-link connecting the candidate YouTube IDs was captured.
The user-requested public-video inventory must remain uncreated until channel ownership and the Camila/Kamilah/Camilla name relationship are established.

resolution.conclusion: The search surfaced multiple similarly branded YouTube channels and external profiles, but no first-party cross-link proves they belong to one creator. A transcript spelling 'Camila' alongside a channel attribution 'Kamilah' is a lead, not proof. Do not combine channels, attribute videos, or create an exhaustive inventory.
required_identity_evidence: A creator-controlled official website that links to the exact YouTube channel ID/handle.
A verified social account linked from the YouTube About page and linking back to the same channel.
A direct creator statement or platform verification that resolves the Kamilah/Camila/Camilla spelling.
If legal identity matters, a public business/entity record matching the creator's own disclosed identity.

competing_hypotheses.claim: The two channel IDs and external accounts belong to one creator operating multiple channels.
evidence_for: Similar branding and near-identical channel descriptions.
evidence_against: No first-party cross-links; channel IDs differ; third-party metrics and identity strings conflict.

competing_hypotheses.claim: Some similarly branded channels or social accounts are mirrors, fan accounts, SEO clones or impersonators.
evidence_for: Multiple channels and handles use similar names/descriptions; third-party directories list many near-duplicates.
evidence_against: No direct evidence of impersonation or unauthorized use.

competing_hypotheses.claim: The speaker's 'Camila' pronunciation/spelling and the channel's 'Kamilah' branding refer to the same person.
evidence_for: Third-party transcripts repeatedly show the spoken introduction 'Camila Stevenson' on videos attributed to Kamilah.
evidence_against: No creator-controlled legal or profile statement explains the spelling difference.

video_inventory_policy.reason: First-party channel identity and ownership not verified.
video_inventory_policy.allowed_until_verified: Retain candidate channel IDs and identity evidence only; do not compile, attribute or present a video list.

source_quality.raw_receipts: No byte-complete raw page captures or SHA-256 receipts.

next_actions: Keep all candidate channel IDs separate in the entity graph.
Search only for creator-controlled cross-links and official channel ownership evidence; do not use subscriber counts, copied descriptions or third-party AI scores as identity proof.
Once one canonical channel is verified, inventory only that channel's public videos and preserve upload dates, canonical video IDs, source capture times and creator attribution evidence.
